mainTopic: Defining העראה: its sources, the three uses of 'שכבת זרע', and the reports of רבי יוחנן about what counts as העראה and גמר ביאה
overview: The amud opens by finishing a list of sources showing that הַעֲרָאָה (the first stage of relations) counts as full ביאה. A גזרה שוה of 'ביאה' covers prohibitions and יבום, and a גזרה שוה of 'קיחה' covers קידושין. Then רבא asks why the תורה writes 'שכבת זרע' by שפחה חרופה, by אשת איש, and by סוטה. By שפחה חרופה it requires a complete act. By אשת איש it excludes relations with a dead woman. By סוטה, after the attempts of רב ששת, רבא and אביי, the גמרא concludes that a husband's warning about mere closeness 'by way of limbs' does not count. Next, שמואל defines העראה as outer contact ('kissing'). Several sages then bring different reports of רבי יוחנן's view. רבה בר בר חנה says הכנסת עטרה is a complete act with a שפחה חרופה. רב דימי, רבין and רב שמואל בר יהודה say it is only העראה, and that גמר ביאה is literally a complete act.

steps.title: Prohibitions from a positive command are learned from the word 'entering'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer to the earlier question about חייבי עשה. A גזרה שוה of the word 'ביאה' teaches that העראה counts for them just as it does for regular prohibitions.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is learned from the word 'entering' here and the word 'entering' there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering a question it asked just before this point: how do we know that העראה counts as ביאה for prohibitions that come from a positive command? Its answer is a word-link between two פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'יבא' (shall enter) appears in the פסוק about a ממזר, which is a regular לאו. It also appears in the פסוק about the third generation of מצרי and אדומי converts, which is an עשה-type prohibition. Because the same word appears in both, the two areas are joined, and the rule of העראה carries over from the לאו to the עשה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It comes': it is learned from
Entering; here, the word used for intimacy and for entering the community
A rule learned because the same word appears in two places in the תורה
The first stage of intimacy, before it is complete
People forbidden to marry because of a prohibition that comes from a positive command

phrases.english: It is derived from 'entering' and 'entering.'
phrases.notes: The two פסוקים are דברים 23:3 (a ממזר 'shall not enter') and דברים 23:9 (the third generation 'may enter').

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer to the question about חייבי עשה, which the גמרא asked just before this section.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזרה שוה of 'ביאה' links עשה-type prohibitions to regular לאוין, so the rule of העראה applies to both.

steps.title: Asking about a יבמה with an outside man
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that העראה counts as ביאה when a יבמה is with a man from outside the family.
steps.simpleTranslation: A יבמה with a man from the general public: from where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next case on its list. It asks for a source that העראה counts when a יבמה, who is waiting for יבום, is with an outside man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יבמה may not marry anyone outside the family until there is יבום or חליצה. The question assumes this case might need its own source, the way the earlier cases did.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow whose husband died without children, waiting for יבום or חליצה
'To the market': to an outside man from the general public
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: A yevama to the general public, from where do we derive it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next case in the series of questions about העראה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that העראה counts as forbidden ביאה for a יבמה with an outside man.

steps.title: No separate source is needed for the יבמה and the outside man
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets the question aside. Whichever view you hold, this case is either a לאו or an עשה, and both of those were already covered.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you follow the view that it is a לאו, it is a לאו like any other. If you follow the view that it is an עשה, it is an עשה like any other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the question from the last step is not really a question. This case already fits into a category that has a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a מחלוקת about whether the ban on a יבמה with an outsider is a לאו or an עשה. Either way, the גמרא has already shown that העראה counts for both לאוין and עשה-type prohibitions. So nothing new needs to be learned.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says
A negative prohibition
A positive command, or a prohibition that comes from one

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying that a יבמה with an outsider is allowed. It is only saying that the question needs no new source, because this case is already covered by the general rules.

phrases.english: If according to the one who says it is a prohibition, it is a prohibition,
if according to the one who says it is a positive מצוה, it is a positive מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets aside the question of step 2 by placing the case inside categories that are already covered.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The need for a separate source for a יבמה with an outside man.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case is already covered by the sources for לאוין and עשה, whichever view one holds.

steps.title: The real question: how a יבם acquires through העראה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords the question. The real question is where we learn that a יבם acquires his יבמה through העראה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, a יבמה to her יבם: from where do we learn it?
steps.whatsHappening: The word 'אלא' tells us the גמרא is changing the question. It now asks about acquiring the יבמה through יבום, not about something forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier questions were all about forbidden relations. This one asks something different: does העראה have the power to complete יבום? That needs a new source, because no prohibition is involved here.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: a sign that the question is being changed
The brother of the man who died, who does יבום
Acquiring; here, the יבם completing the marriage

phrases.english: Rather: a yevama to her yavam, from where do we derive it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the question that was set aside with the question that truly needs a source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that a יבם acquires his יבמה through העראה.

steps.title: יבום is also learned from 'entering'
steps.stepSummary: A גזרה שוה of 'ביאה' links the פסוק about יבום to the prohibition פסוקים, so העראה is enough to complete יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is learned from the word 'entering' here and the word 'entering' there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word 'יבא' in the פסוק about יבום links it to the other 'ביאה' פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know that העראה counts as ביאה in the prohibitions. The same word in the פסוק about יבום carries that rule over, so the יבם acquires her through העראה. Notice that the גמרא's words here are exactly the same as in step 1, but now they answer a different question.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Her יבם shall come upon her': the פסוק about יבום

steps.whatToRemember: The single word 'ביאה' ties together the prohibitions and יבום. Because of it, העראה counts in both areas.

phrases.english: It is derived from 'entering' and 'entering.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the reworded question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזרה שוה of 'ביאה' between יבום and the prohibitions.

steps.title: Asking about קידושין through העראה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that a woman becomes מקודשת to her husband through העראה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman to her husband: from where do we learn it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case: קידושין done through ביאה. Does העראה alone work?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like יבום, this question is about making a marriage take effect, not about a prohibition. So it needs its own source.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman to her husband: becoming his wife
The first stage of marriage (betrothal)

phrases.english: A woman to her husband, from where do we derive it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list with a new case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that העראה makes a woman מקודשת to her husband.

steps.title: קידושין is learned from the word 'taking'
steps.stepSummary: A גזרה שוה of 'קיחה' links קידושין to the forbidden relations, so העראה works for קידושין too.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is learned from the word 'taking' here and the word 'taking' there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a different word-link, 'קיחה' (taking). It joins the פסוק about marriage to a פסוק about forbidden relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about marriage says 'כי יקח איש'. A פסוק about forbidden relations also uses 'יקח', and there העראה counts. So in קידושין, העראה counts as well. A different word is used here because the marriage פסוק says 'taking', not 'entering'.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking: the word the תורה uses for marriage
'When a man takes': the פסוק about marriage

steps.whatToRemember: There are two word-links in this section. 'ביאה' covers the prohibitions and יבום, and 'קיחה' covers קידושין. Through both, העראה counts as full ביאה.

phrases.english: It is derived from 'taking' and 'taking.'
phrases.notes: The two פסוקים are דברים 24:1 (marriage) and ויקרא 20:17 (taking one's sister).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזרה שוה of 'קיחה' between קידושין and the forbidden relations.

steps.title: Why is 'cohabitation with seed' written three times?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks why the תורה uses the words 'שכבת זרע' by שפחה חרופה, by אשת איש, and by סוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Why do I need the words 'שכבת זרע' that the תורה wrote by a שפחה חרופה, by an אשת איש, and by a סוטה?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new question. We just learned that העראה counts as ביאה, so what do these three uses of 'שכבת זרע' come to teach?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'שכבת זרע' sounds like it needs a complete act. Since העראה already counts, each of the three places must be teaching something else. רבא wants to know what each one teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: Cohabitation with seed; relations that can produce a child
A half-freed maidservant who is designated to a Jewish man
A married woman
A wife suspected of adultery after her husband warned her
The Merciful One; a name for ה׳ as the Author of the תורה

phrases.english: Rava said:
Why do I need that the Merciful One wrote
"cohabitation with seed" by a designated maidservant,
phrases.notes: The three פסוקים are ויקרא 19:20, ויקרא 18:20, and במדבר 5:13.

phrases.english: "cohabitation with seed" by a married woman,
and "cohabitation with seed" by a sotah?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לְמָה לִי דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion that העראה counts as ביאה and asks what the extra words teach.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What each of the three 'שכבת זרע' phrases comes to teach.

steps.title: The maidservant as explained; the married woman excludes a limp organ
steps.stepSummary: By שפחה חרופה the phrase means what was already said. By אשת איש it excludes relations with a limp, 'dead' organ.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one by שפחה חרופה is as we said. The one by אשת איש excludes someone who has relations with a 'dead' organ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers two of the three. For שפחה חרופה it points back to an earlier explanation, and for אשת איש it offers a new purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By שפחה חרופה, the phrase limits punishment to a complete act. By אשת איש, 'זרע' (seed) is used to exclude relations that cannot lead to a child, such as with a limp organ.

keyTerms.meaning: As we said earlier
To exclude; this comes to leave out a certain case
One who has relations with a limp, non-erect organ

phrases.english: The one by a designated maidservant is as we said.
phrases.notes: This points back to 55a: with her, only a complete act brings punishment, not just העראה.

phrases.english: The one by a married woman
excludes one who has relations with a dead organ.
phrases.notes: 'Dead' here means the man's organ is not erect, so these relations can't produce a child.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question for the first two cases.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שפחה חרופה: only a complete act is punished. אשת איש: excludes משמש מת.

steps.title: This answer fails for the view that a limp organ still makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: The אשת איש answer only works for the view that משמש מת is exempt. What about the view that he is liable?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the one who says that משמש מת with forbidden relations is exempt. But for the one who says he is liable, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer just given for אשת איש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a dispute about whether משמש מת counts as relations with עריות. If he is liable, the פסוק can't be excluding him, so the extra words by אשת איש need a different purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well for the one who says
Forbidden relations
What is there to say? (the answer doesn't work)

phrases.english: This works well for the one who says
that one who has relations with a dead organ with forbidden relations is exempt,
but according to the one who says he is liable,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation given for אשת איש.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'שכבת זרע' by אשת איש excludes משמש מת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to the view that משמש מת is liable, the פסוק cannot be excluding him.

steps.title: New answer: the married-woman phrase excludes relations with a dead woman
steps.stepSummary: Rather, the phrase by אשת איש excludes relations with a dead woman. Without it, we might think she is still his wife after death.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it excludes relations with a dead woman. You might have thought that since she is still called 'שארו' (his kin) after death, one would be liable for her as an אשת איש. So the פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא replaces its earlier answer with a new purpose for 'שכבת זרע' by אשת איש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wife is still called her husband's 'שארו' even after she dies, so one could think relations with her still count as אשת איש. 'שכבת זרע' teaches that relations with a dead woman are not considered relations at all for this איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: One who has relations with a dead woman
You might have thought to say
His kin; a term for a man's wife
It teaches us (that the thought is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: By אשת איש, 'שכבת זרע' excludes relations with a dead woman: even though she is still called her husband's 'שארו', there is no אשת איש liability.

phrases.english: Rather: it excludes one who has relations with a dead woman.
For it might enter your mind to say:
Since after death
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in square brackets, 'since', and some don't.

phrases.english: she is also called "his kin,"
say that one should be liable for her as a married woman,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected explanation from step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of what the פסוק excludes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a dead wife is still called 'שארו', relations with her would bring אשת איש liability.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'שכבת זרע' excludes a dead woman, so there is no אשת איש liability for her.

steps.title: Why is the phrase needed by sotah?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the third case and asks why 'שכבת זרע' is written by סוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need the one written by סוטה?
steps.whatsHappening: Having handled two cases, the גמרא now asks about the third one, סוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats רבא's original question, now aimed only at the פסוק by סוטה. The answer will come from a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it?

phrases.english: Why do I need the one by a sotah?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the third case from רבא's question.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the phrase excludes 'something else'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that 'שכבת זרע' by סוטה excludes 'something else'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for what the ברייתא teaches: 'שכבת זרע' excludes something else.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא's wording is vague, which sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the phrase leaves out some case, but it doesn't say which one. The גמרא will need to explain what 'something else' means.

keyTerms.meaning: As was taught in a ברייתא
Something else; here a vague phrase that needs explaining

phrases.english: For that which was taught:
"Cohabitation with seed" excludes something else.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about סוטה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא says the phrase excludes 'something else'.

steps.title: What does 'something else' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means by 'something else'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'something else'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the vague phrase in the ברייתא. This sets up רב ששת's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'דבר אחר' is a vague phrase that often refers to something delicate. The גמרא wants to know exactly which case the ברייתא is leaving out.

keyTerms.meaning: What is?

phrases.english: What is "something else"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the ברייתא's words.

steps.title: רב ששת: a warning about unnatural relations
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the phrase excludes a case where the husband warned his wife against unnatural relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: It excludes a case where the husband warned her about unnatural relations.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת explains 'something else'. If the warning (קינוי) was about unnatural relations, the סוטה laws don't apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since 'שכבת זרע' means relations that can produce a child, רב ששת reads it as limiting the קינוי to natural relations. A warning about the other kind would not make her a סוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: He warned her (the husband's warning that starts the סוטה process)
Not in the usual way; unnatural relations

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
It excludes where he warned her
about relations not in the usual way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: פְּרָט לְשֶׁקִּינֵּא לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers what 'דבר אחר' means.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It excludes a קינוי about unnatural relations.

steps.title: רבא objects: 'the lyings of a woman' includes both ways
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב ששת: the פסוק says 'משכבי אשה' (plural), which shows both kinds of relations count with a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: But it is written 'משכבי אשה', the lyings of a woman!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב ששת's explanation. The next step shows that רב ששת's reading is dropped, and רבא offers his own explanation of 'something else'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural 'משכבי' teaches that there are two ways of having relations with a woman, and both are treated the same. So how could a warning about unnatural relations be excluded for סוטה?

keyTerms.meaning: The lyings of a woman; the plural shows two kinds of relations
It is written

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
"The lyings of a woman" is written!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:22. The plural 'lyings' tells us both ways of relations with a woman count the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's explanation.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's claim that a קינוי about unnatural relations is excluded.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plural 'משכבי אשה' makes both kinds of relations equal, so unnatural relations should count for סוטה too.

steps.title: רבא's new explanation: a warning about closeness through other limbs
steps.stepSummary: רבא suggests that 'שכבת זרע' excludes a case where the husband warned his wife only against physical closeness through other body parts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: The words exclude a case where the husband warned her about closeness 'by way of limbs'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת's answer was just rejected, so רבא offers a new answer to the question: what is the 'something else' that the ברייתא says is excluded?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קינוי (warning) only makes a woman a סוטה if it warns against real relations. רבא says the תורה's word 'שכבת זרע' teaches that a warning about mere physical closeness with other limbs does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, to leave out (this case)
That he warned her (gave her a jealous warning)
By way of limbs: physical closeness without actual relations

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
It excludes a case where he warned her
about contact by way of limbs.
phrases.notes: He means close physical contact with other body parts, not actual relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב ששת's rejected explanation with a new one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does 'something else' in the ברייתא refer to?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A warning about closeness by way of other limbs.

steps.title: אביי objects: the Torah never forbids mere immodesty
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks: does the תורה make a woman forbidden just for immodest behavior? Of course not, so why would we need a word to exclude it?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Did the תורה forbid just immodest behavior?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Physical closeness without relations never makes a woman forbidden to her husband. So a warning about it obviously cannot make her a סוטה, and the תורה would not need a special word to teach that.

keyTerms.meaning: Loose, immodest behavior
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Did the Merciful One forbid her because of mere immodest behavior?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's explanation in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that 'שכבת זרע' excludes a warning about closeness by way of limbs.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That case is obvious, because immodesty alone never forbids a woman, so no verse is needed to exclude it.

steps.title: אביי's explanation: a warning about 'kissing'
steps.stepSummary: אביי suggests that the words exclude a warning about 'kissing', meaning outer contact of the bodies without entering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: It excludes a case where he warned her about 'kissing'.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected רבא's case, אביי offers his own answer to what 'something else' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי chooses a case that is closer to real relations, so it is not obvious. That makes it worth a special word in the תורה to teach that this kind of warning does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'kiss'; here, outer contact of the bodies without entering

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
It excludes a case where he warned her about 'kissing'.
phrases.notes: 'Kissing' here isn't a kiss on the lips. It means the bodies touch on the outside, without entering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new explanation after אביי rejected רבא's.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does 'something else' in the ברייתא refer to?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A warning about 'kissing', meaning outer contact.

steps.title: אביי's answer only works for one opinion about העראה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that אביי's answer works if העראה means entering a little, but not if העראה means 'kissing' itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the one who says העראה is when the crown enters. But for the one who says העראה is 'kissing', what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's explanation by showing it depends on a disagreement about what העראה is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If העראה starts only when the body enters, then 'kissing' is not relations, and a warning about it should not count. But if 'kissing' itself is העראה, then it is real relations and a warning about it should count. So it cannot be the case the Torah excludes.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well for the one who says
The first stage of relations
Entering of the crown: a small amount of entering
What is there to say?

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says
the first stage of relations is the entering of the crown.
But according to the one who says it is 'kissing',
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's explanation in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that 'שכבת זרע' excludes a warning about 'kissing'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to the view that 'kissing' is itself העראה, it counts as real relations, so a warning about it should make her a סוטה.

steps.title: Back to רבא: the verse was needed because of the husband's objection
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רבא's case and explains why it was needed: we might have thought that whatever the husband objects to is enough for a warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, really it is a warning about closeness by way of limbs. And it was needed, because you might have thought the Torah made it depend on the husband's objection, and here he does object. So the verse teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבא's explanation and answers אביי's challenge from step 18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said a warning about immodesty is obviously meaningless. The גמרא answers that it is not obvious: since the husband is the one who chooses to warn, maybe anything he objects to would count. The word 'שכבת זרע' teaches that the warning must be about real relations.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (going back to an earlier idea)
It was necessary
It might have entered your mind to say
Objection, strictness
It teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: In the end, 'שכבת זרע' by סוטה teaches that a warning only counts if it is about real relations. A warning about closeness 'by way of limbs' does not count, even though the husband objects to it.
steps.confusionAlert: This step does not reject אביי's point that closeness alone never forbids a woman. It only explains why we still needed the verse: the warning is the husband's choice, so we might have thought his objection was enough.

phrases.english: Rather, really
it is a case where he warned her about contact by way of limbs,
and it was necessary to teach it,
because it might have entered your mind to say:
the Merciful One made it depend on the husband's objection,
and here he does object,
so it teaches us that this does not count.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לְעוֹלָם לְשֶׁקִּינֵּא לָהּ דֶּרֶךְ אֵבָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Drops אביי's explanation and defends רבא's against אביי's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the case is not obvious, so the verse is needed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the warning depends on the husband, any behavior he objects to would make his warning count.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a warning about real relations counts. A warning about mere closeness by way of limbs does not.

steps.title: שמואל: העראה is 'kissing', like a finger on the lips
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that העראה is 'kissing' (outer contact), and explains with a parable that outer contact always involves a little pressing in.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: העראה is 'kissing'. It is like a person who puts his finger on his mouth: he cannot avoid pressing the flesh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings שמואל's statement on the question from step 20: what exactly counts as העראה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל holds the view that 'kissing' itself is העראה. His parable explains why: just as a finger on the lips always presses them a little, outer contact always includes a tiny bit of entering, so it counts as relations.

keyTerms.meaning: A comparison, a parable
His finger
It is impossible
He will press

steps.whyThisMatters: שמואל is the one who holds the opinion mentioned in step 20, which is why אביי's explanation could not stand according to everyone.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
The first stage of relations is 'kissing'.

phrases.aramaic: מָשָׁל לְאָדָם שֶׁמַּנִּיחַ אֶצְבָּעוֹ עַל פִּיו,
phrases.english: It is like a person who places his finger on his mouth;
it is impossible that he not press the flesh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to defining העראה, the disagreement raised in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: העראה is outer contact ('kissing'), because such contact always presses in a little.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה reports רבי יוחנן's definition of a complete act
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה quotes רבי יוחנן: for a שפחה חרופה, a complete act (גמר ביאה) means הכנסת עטרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבה בר בר חנה came from ארץ ישראל, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the 'complete act' mentioned for a שפחה חרופה means entering as far as the עטרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new report of רבי יוחנן's view, which רבה בר בר חנה brought back from ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case of a שפחה חרופה requires a complete act, not just העראה. רבי יוחנן says that 'complete' is reached already at הכנסת עטרה. Full entry is not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
A complete act of relations
A designated maidservant, half-freed and promised to a man
Entering as far as the crown (the tip)

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה,
phrases.english: When Rabba bar bar Ḥana came,
he said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The complete act stated regarding a designated maidservant
is the insertion of the corona.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After שמואל defined העראה, the גמרא now brings רבי יוחנן's definitions of the stages of the act.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For שפחה חרופה, גמר ביאה = הכנסת עטרה.

steps.title: רב ששת challenges from the words 'שכבת זרע'
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת cites a ברייתא: liability with a שפחה חרופה applies only to a 'finished' act (ביאת המירוק). Doesn't that mean full entry of the whole organ?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת objected: The ברייתא learns from 'שכבת זרע' that a person is liable only for a finished act. Doesn't 'finished' mean the whole organ entered fully?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת attacks רבה בר בר חנה's report using a ברייתא about the שפחה חרופה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא requires a 'מירוק', a finished act. רב ששת assumes this means the whole organ entered. If so, entering only to the עטרה would not be enough, which contradicts the report in רבי יוחנן's name.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Lying with seed', the Torah's wording for the שפחה חרופה case
A finished act of relations
The whole organ

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet raised an objection:
'Cohabitation with seed',

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא עַל בִּיאַת הַמֵּירוּק.
phrases.english: one is liable only for a completed act.
Doesn't this mean completion of the whole member?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה בר בר חנה's report of רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that גמר ביאה = הכנסת עטרה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'מירוק' sounds like full entry of the whole organ, so הכנסת עטרה should not be enough.

steps.title: 'Finished' means finishing the עטרה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: no, מירוק can mean finishing the entry of the עטרה, not of the whole organ.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means the עטרה is fully entered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבה בר בר חנה's report by reading the ברייתא differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מירוק' does not have to mean the whole organ. It can mean the עטרה went in completely. That is exactly הכנסת עטרה, so the ברייתא fits רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Complete entry of the עטרה

phrases.english: No, completion of the corona.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ששת's challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מירוק means full entry of the whole organ.
steps.terutzMaskana: מירוק means full entry of the עטרה, which matches רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: רב דימי reports that הכנסת עטרה is only העראה
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי quotes רבי יוחנן: העראה, the first stage, is הכנסת עטרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: העראה means entering as far as the עטרה.
steps.whatsHappening: A second scholar brings a different report of what רבי יוחנן said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here הכנסת עטרה is called העראה, only the beginning stage. According to רבה בר בר חנה, the same amount counted as a complete act. So the two reports seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: The first stage of relations, short of a complete act

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came,
he said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The initial stage is the insertion of the corona.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, apparently conflicting report of רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: The listeners point out the contradiction
steps.stepSummary: They tell רב דימי that רבה בר בר חנה did not quote רבי יוחנן this way.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: But רבה בר בר חנה did not say this!
steps.whatsHappening: The listeners challenge רב דימי by pointing to the earlier report.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר בר חנה said הכנסת עטרה is a complete act. רב דימי says it is only העראה. Both cannot be accurate quotes of the same teacher.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely... (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: They said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה לָא אָמַר הָכִי!
phrases.english: But Rabba bar bar Ḥana did not say so!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: וְהָא רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה לָא אָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב דימי's report.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's report of רבי יוחנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It contradicts רבה בר בר חנה's report of the same teacher.

steps.title: רב דימי: one of us quoted wrongly
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי admits the reports cannot be reconciled. One of the two quoted רבי יוחנן wrongly.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Either he is wrong or I am wrong.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי answers the challenge by admitting it is a real contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not try to make the reports fit together. He openly says one report must be mistaken.

keyTerms.meaning: Spoke falsely, here meaning quoted incorrectly

steps.confusionAlert: 'שקראי' does not accuse anyone of lying on purpose. It means one of the two quotes is simply inaccurate.

phrases.english: He said to them:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אִיהוּ שַׁקְרַאי אוֹ אֲנָא שַׁקְרַי.
phrases.english: Either he lied or I am lying.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ אִיהוּ שַׁקְרַאי אוֹ אֲנָא שַׁקְרַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the challenge by conceding the contradiction.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The reports truly conflict, and one is inaccurate.

steps.title: רבין gives the same report as רב דימי
steps.stepSummary: רבין also quotes רבי יוחנן: העראה is הכנסת עטרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came from ארץ ישראל, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: העראה means entering as far as the עטרה.
steps.whatsHappening: A third scholar arrives and agrees with רב דימי's version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now two reports say הכנסת עטרה is only העראה, against רבה בר בר חנה. This sets up the next question: how does this fit with שמואל?

phrases.english: When Ravin came,
he said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The initial stage is the insertion of the corona.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב דימי's version.

steps.title: Does רבין's report disagree with שמואל too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבין surely disagrees with רבה בר בר חנה, then asks whether he also disagrees with שמואל, who defined העראה as outer contact.
steps.simpleTranslation: He certainly disagrees with רבה בר בר חנה. But should we say he also disagrees with שמואל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts one conflict and asks about a second possible conflict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With רבה בר בר חנה the conflict is clear: is הכנסת עטרה a complete act or only העראה? With שמואל (step 22), the question is whether העראה is outer contact or entering to the עטרה.

keyTerms.meaning: He certainly disagrees
Shall we say...? (opens a suggestion that is often rejected)

phrases.aramaic: אַדְּרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה וַדַּאי פְּלִיג.
phrases.english: With Rabba bar bar Ḥana he certainly disagrees.
Shall we say he disagrees with Shmuel?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares רבין's report with earlier opinions.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי יוחנן's definition of העראה (in רבין's version) conflict with שמואל's?

steps.title: From outer contact up to the עטרה is all העראה
steps.stepSummary: No conflict with שמואל: everything from outer contact up to הכנסת עטרה is called העראה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everything from outer contact until entering to the עטרה is called העראה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן and שמואל do not really disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן was giving the upper limit of העראה, and שמואל was giving where it begins. Together they define one range: from outer contact through הכנסת עטרה. Anything beyond that is a complete act.

keyTerms.meaning: From outer contact until...
He calls it

steps.whatToRemember: There are two reports of רבי יוחנן: רבה בר בר חנה says הכנסת עטרה is a complete act, while רב דימי and רבין say it is only העראה. In רבין's version, העראה covers everything from outer contact up to הכנסת עטרה, so it fits with שמואל.

phrases.english: No, from a kiss until the insertion of the corona —
phrases.notes: 'Kiss' here is שמואל's word for outer contact without entering.

phrases.english: he calls it the initial stage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by making רבין's report fit with שמואל.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: העראה is a range: from outer contact up to הכנסת עטרה. שמואל gave its start and רבי יוחנן gave its end.

steps.title: רב שמואל בר יהודה's report: העראה and גמר ביאה defined
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר יהודה quotes רבי יוחנן: העראה is הכנסת עטרה, and גמר ביאה is a truly complete act.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב שמואל בר יהודה came from ארץ ישראל, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: העראה is הכנסת עטרה, and a complete act (גמר ביאה) means literally a complete act.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more report of what רבי יוחנן said, this time from רב שמואל בר יהודה. It gives the same definition of העראה that רבין gave, and adds a definition of גמר ביאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This report backs up רבין's quote that העראה means הכנסת עטרה. It also adds something new: גמר ביאה is not just a bit more than העראה. It is literally a full act, which goes beyond the הכנסת עטרה stage.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came. The usual phrase for a sage arriving from ארץ ישראל with a teaching from there.
The first stage of relations.
Insertion of the corona.
A complete act of relations.
Literally, truly.

steps.whatToRemember: According to this report of רבי יוחנן, there are two stages: העראה means הכנסת עטרה, and גמר ביאה means a literally complete act beyond that.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: When Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda came
he said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The initial stage is the insertion of the corona,
a complete act is literally a complete act.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further report of רבי יוחנן that matches רבין's definition of העראה and adds a definition of גמר ביאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the name of רבי יוחנן: העראה is הכנסת עטרה, and גמר ביאה is a literally complete act.
